description: The position is described below. If you want to apply, click the Apply Now button at the top or bottom of this page. After you click Apply Now and complete your application, you'll be invited to create a profile, which will let you see your application status and any communications. If you already have a profile with us, you can log in to check status. Need Help? If you have a disability and need assistance with the application, you can request a reasonable accommodation. Send an email to Accessibility (accommodation requests only; other inquiries won't receive a response). Regular or Temporary: Regular Language Fluency: English (Required) Work Shift: 1st shift (United States of America) Please review the following job description: Truist Audit Manager is responsible for providing a leadership role in the delivery of high-risk, complex and value-added independent and objective risk-based internal audit assurance and advisory services. The Audit Manager will proactively coach junior team members by providing candid and constructive feedback. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Following is a summary of the essential functions for this job. Other duties may be performed, both major and minor, which are not mentioned below. Specific activities may change from time to time. 1. Serve as Engagement Manager of high risk and more complex audit engagements by planning, scoping and developing the test plan, including incorporating the use of data analytics. Effectively allocate resources and individuals in accordance with skills and schedules, to complete assignments within budget. 2. Set clear quality expectations based on Truist Audit Services standards and analyze/review process documentation to evaluate effectiveness and efficiency. 3. Develop meaningful, relevant, and well-supported audit reports that align with Truist's risk appetite framework and present these reports to key department stakeholders. 4. Identify substantive and material issues that go beyond paperwork shortcomings. Ability to look beyond the obvious; finds solutions, not just problems. 5. Provide coaching and guidance in development of junior team members by taking an active role in training and mentoring. 6. Demonstrate effective challenge by providing deep subject matter knowledge industry related knowledge to support business partnership efforts. 7. Manage timely and quality delivery of multiple tasks, including audits, projects and special assignments. Provide advisory services, as necessary, in the implementation of new systems, processes and changes to existing systems, standards and procedures. 8. Ability to work independently while exercising judgement in risk-based assessments difficult or complex nature. QUALIFICATIONS Required Qualifications: The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 1. Bachelor’s degree in accounting, business or related field or equivalent education and related training or experience. 2. Six to eight years of banking, auditing or other relevant experience related to area of responsibility. 3. Strong knowledge, ability and expertise in audit and other areas of banking and financial services. 4. Strong understanding of risk management and process concepts. 5. Strong analytical, facilitation, and interpersonal skills. 6. Demonstrated ability to grasp and communicate the underlying concepts in complex information. 7. Demonstrated ability to identify and communicate root causes of problems. 8. Demonstrated ability to formulate and communicate solutions based on a synthesis of information. 9. Strong written, verbal and negotiating skills. 10. Demonstrated strong proficiency in computer applications and proven experience with tools such as Microsoft Office software products. 11. Strong project management and advisory skills. Preferred Qualifications: 1. Advanced degree. 2. Possess appropriate professional certification. 3. Possess knowledge of Truist Audit Services audit software and business specific software. General Description of Available Benefits for Eligible Employees of Truist Financial Corporation: All regular teammates (not temporary or contingent workers) working 20 hours or more per week are eligible for benefits, though eligibility for specific benefits may be determined by the division of Truist offering the position. Truist offers medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability, accidental death and dismemberment, tax-preferred savings accounts, and a 401k plan to teammates. title: Risk Assurance Manager
description: 🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone. We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking. After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as  personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts , accounts for 16-17 year olds , a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save , invest and  combine their pensions with us.  With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers! We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️   📍Barcelona, Spain  |💰 €53,000 - €65,000, Incentive Awards tied to your performance ➕ benefits | Hear from the team   ⭐Our Risk and Compliance team Monzo Bank Europe (MBEU) is the Irish-based subsidiary of the Monzo Group and the strategic launchpad for our expansion across the European Union. We are looking for a seasoned Risk Assurance Manager to provide independent Second-Line of Defence (2LOD) assurance over the design and effectiveness of the bank’s risk management framework, controls and processes. You will ensure that key risks are managed in line with regulatory expectations, internal policies and our risk appetite, providing robust oversight and challenge across the full spectrum of the bank’s risk universe. In this role, you will ensure the bank complies with: Irish Regulatory Obligations, including CBI, CPC, AML/CFT legislation, and the Companies Act. EU Regulatory Requirements, including DORA, EBA Guidelines, ECB/SSM expectations, and GDPR. Internal Governance, including adherence to risk frameworks, policies, and risk appetite. Reporting directly to the Director of Risk Assurance, MBEU, you will design, execute, and report on 2LOD assurance reviews covering conduct, financial crime, fraud, credit, and financial risks. Your remit will also include operational risk, ICT and information security, outsourcing, data protection and governance structures. This role is critical in fostering a sound risk culture and supporting senior management and the Board in their oversight responsibilities.You will be instrumental in providing stakeholders with the assurance needed to ensure our growth is safe, resilient and compliant. The role you are applying for is a Controlled Function (CF-2) within the meaning of the Central Bank Reform Act, 2010. For this role, appointment will be conditional on Monzo being fully satisfied that the appointee meets the requirements as set out in the Fitness and Probity Standards 2018 issued by the Central Bank of Ireland. As a CF, the role holder will be subject to Conduct Standards under the Central Bank of Ireland Individual Accountability Framework and will be required to take reasonable steps to ensure that the relevant conduct standards are met. 🔑You’ll play a key role by... Assurance Plan: Planning, coordinating and executing comprehensive risk assurance activities, including effectiveness reviews to ensure EU-wide adherence to the enterprise risk framework. Thematic Reviews: Conducting targeted thematic reviews across specific risk areas (e.g., conduct, compliance, financial crime, IT, prudential and strategic risk) to provide in-depth assurance over design adequacy and operating effectiveness. Remediation: Identifying areas for improvement within the risk management framework and control environment, recommending practical, impactful solutions and tracking remediation efforts to completion. Stakeholder Engagement: Proactively engage with business and risk stakeholders to understand Monzo Europe’s products and risk profiles, fostering a collaborative and transparent risk culture. Strategic Planning: Contributing to the annual risk assurance plan by providing insights gathered through continuous monitoring of regulatory trends and horizon scanning, market practices and upstream developments. Framework Governance: Contribute to the continuous improvement of the 2LOD Risk Assurance Framework, Methodology and Terms of Reference to ensure they remain fit-for-purpose and market-leading. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partnering closely with First-Line of Defence (1LOD) control testing, Group 2LOD, and Internal Audit to ensure alignment while maintaining strict independent challenge. Reporting & Governance: Contributing to risk governance by reporting thematic insights, trends and remediation progress to senior management committees. title: AI Security and Data Protection Governance and Control, VP
description: Who We Are Looking For We are looking for a team leader to lead AI Security and Data Protection Governance and Controls, reporting to the Global Head of Data Protection. You will set the enterprise strategy and accountability model for secure, resilient, and responsible AI and data protection capabilities, translating emerging risk into business-aligned policies, standards, controls, investment priorities, and measurable outcomes. You will lead a multidisciplinary team and partner with senior leaders across Security, Technology, Risk, Compliance, Legal, Procurement, Internal Audit, and the business to embed security-by-design and scalable governance across enterprise platforms, applications, data, and third-party services. Why This Role is Important To Us The team is part of Global Cybersecurity, a function vital to protecting the confidentiality, integrity, availability, and resilience of the firm's information and technology environment. This leadership role is accountable for anticipating AI, data, and emerging technology risks; establishing a consistent enterprise control posture; directing remediation and transformation priorities; and representing the program with executive leadership, clients, auditors, and regulators. The role will enable the organization to adopt AI and data-driven capabilities securely while maintaining regulatory readiness and sustainable risk reduction. What You Will Be Responsible For In this role, you will: • Set the enterprise vision, strategy, governance model, and multi-year roadmap for AI security, data protection, and emerging technology risk. • Lead, develop, and retain a multidisciplinary team responsible for governance, control oversight, risk assessment, assurance, program execution, and stakeholder engagement. • Establish enterprise policies, standards, control objectives, decision rights, risk ownership, and accountability across AI models, data assets, applications, infrastructure, cloud, identity, networks, and third-party services. • Direct the discovery, inventory, classification, and risk assessment of AI models, sensitive data, security controls, platforms, integrations, and critical technology dependencies. • Approve risk-based prioritization criteria and investment decisions using data sensitivity, business criticality, external exposure, retention, control maturity, regulatory impact, and remediation complexity. • Sponsor minimum control requirements, testing and evidence standards, exception governance, compensating controls, risk acceptance, and remediation expectations across the enterprise. • Oversee the transition of vulnerable or noncompliant implementations to approved secure technologies and control solutions, including milestones, funding, dependencies, control gates, and executive escalation. • Partner with Security Architecture and Engineering leaders to embed AI security, data protection, security-by-design, and adaptable control requirements into architectures, engineering standards, and reusable implementation patterns. • Establish third-party AI security and data protection requirements for products, cloud services, strategic vendors, due diligence, contracts, and ongoing oversight. • Serve as the senior subject-matter authority for AI security and data protection governance in engagements with executive leadership, Risk, Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, external auditors, clients, and regulators. • Define management reporting, key risk indicators, performance measures, and executive dashboards covering inventory, exposure, control compliance, exceptions, remediation, roadmap delivery, and residual risk. • Own program operating rhythm, resource planning, budget priorities, and cross-functional governance to drive timely decisions and measurable risk reduction. What We Value These skills will help you succeed in this role: • Enterprise leadership experience spanning AI security, data protection, security architecture, cybersecurity governance, technology risk, and control transformation. • Ability to convert complex technical, regulatory, and emerging risks into clear enterprise strategy, policy, control requirements, funding priorities, and executive decisions. • Strong judgment in control design, assurance, exception management, risk acceptance, issue remediation, and regulatory engagement within a large, regulated organization. • Proven success leading senior teams and complex, cross-functional transformation programs with measurable outcomes, clear accountability, and sustained adoption. • Executive presence and influence across Security, Engineering, Infrastructure, Cloud, Application Development, Data, Risk, Legal, Procurement, Audit, and business leadership. • Data-driven, risk-based decision making with the ability to balance strategic direction, delivery urgency, regulatory obligations, and operational resilience. • Commitment to developing talent, simplifying governance, standardizing controls, and building scalable operating model

title: Compliance Lead, Testing
description: At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most. About the Legal, Compliance, and Public Affairs team  The Legal, Compliance, and Public Affairs team is a group of dedicated professionals committed to helping Affirm scale, innovate, and provide outstanding products for consumers, merchants, and key partners. We combine legal, compliance, and policy expertise to guide growth, shape products, and build trust across our ecosystem. Our work spans multiple professional disciplines and provides the foundation for Affirm’s mission to deliver honest financial products. About the role Affirm’s Compliance team implements a compliance program that enables Affirm to proactively adhere to regulatory requirements while also identifying and addressing potential regulatory issues that may arise. As a second line of defense, Compliance proactively partners with the business to support new products, markets, initiatives, change management, issue identification and remediation plans, and assessment/monitoring of third parties. Affirm is actively seeking a Compliance Lead to support certain critical compliance management program elements. In this role, the Compliance Lead will help to administer Compliance’s Testing Program. This includes completing reviews to ensure compliance with federal/state regulations, identifying gaps and deficiencies with regulatory compliance concerns, collaborate with cross functional partners including Legal, Operations, Product, Engineering and senior management to resolve identified issues and further build out our compliance program. This role will report to the Senior Compliance Manager and will be required to work independently and cross-functionally. What you'll do Perform ongoing compliance testing and reporting on adherence to compliance program and federal/state regulatory requirements. Work closely and cross-functionally with multiple departments (Compliance, Legal, Risk, Product, etc.) while completing reviews. Support a very fast paced business with tight deadlines while providing diligent and detailed work product. Collaborate with management to identify improvements to current processes or propose new processes to strengthen internal controls. Coordinate the execution of the compliance risk assessment and control inventory, including collecting and documenting results. Serve as an expert in the area of regulatory compliance and how it applies to new and/or revised products and services. Continuously improve internal compliance processes relating to the Compliance Testing Program. What we look for 5+ years of professional work experience in Compliance Testing, or Audit. Knowledge of applicable laws, regulations, financial services, and regulatory trends that impact Affirm’s business. Experience in completing end-to-end compliance testing activities. Strong communication and relationship management skills. Inquisitive and proactive in proposing creative and effective solutions and ability to learn and adapt in a fast-paced environment. Strong project management, critical thinking and analytical skills. Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to clearly present complex and sensitive issues. Proficient computer navigation skills using a variety of software packages, including Google docs, word processing, spreadsheets, and presentations. Must be detail oriented, thorough, and well organized. Base Pay Grade - J Equity Grade - 5 Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills. Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include equity rewards, monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents.) USA base pay range (CA, WA, NY, NJ, CT) per year: $130,000 - $180,000 USA base pay range (all other U.S. states) per year: $115,000 - $165,000 Please note that visa sponsorship is not available for this position. #LI-Remote Remote-first with flexibility built in Affirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience. Benefits designed for you Our benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. title: Senior Manager, Financial Systems & Reporting Transformation
description: ABOUT THE ROLE The Senior Manager, Financial Systems & Reporting Transformation is responsible for leading the redesign of the company's financial master data — including the chart of accounts, cost centers, profit centers, product hierarchies, and dimensional reporting structures — with the objective of enhancing profitability insights, standardizing management reporting, and enabling seamless upstream consolidation with the parent company.  YOUR DAILY IMPACT AT PELOTON Lead the end-to-end redesign of the company's financial master data structures — chart of accounts, cost centers, profit centers, functional areas, internal orders, product hierarchies, customer/vendor master, and reporting dimensions — to enable enhanced profitability, channel, and product-level reporting Define the target-state data model required for seamless consolidation with the parent company's reporting environment, including alignment of GL accounts, entity structures, intercompany conventions, and dimensional hierarchies Develop and execute the migration plan from the legacy fragmented environment to the redesigned master data model, including data mapping, cleansing, cutover, and validation Establish master data governance (ownership, request/approval workflows, change controls, and audit trails) to preserve data integrity post-implementation Partner with IT and the SAP functional teams to configure and validate master data changes in SAP ECC, ensuring downstream impacts to sub-ledgers, allocations, and reporting are fully understood and controlled Spearhead process optimization efforts within key functional areas, including the month-end close process, consolidations, allocations, and monthly management reporting Drive efficiency and process design improvements within major transaction cycles: Order to Cash (OTC), Procure to Pay (PTP), Inventory, and Fixed Assets — with particular focus on how master data drives accuracy, controls, and reporting granularity Identify, champion, and execute opportunities to leverage IT solutions — SAP ECC configuration, reporting layers, and complementary tools — to create efficiencies and strengthen internal controls Collaborate directly with global and regional business leaders to drive actionable roadmaps for process simplification and automation, ensuring solutions are pragmatic and scalable Serve as the lead point of contact for financial data alignment with the parent company, ensuring the redesigned master data supports consolidated reporting, elimination entries, and management-view analytics Partner with the parent company's controllership and FP&A teams to define mapping rules, submission cadences, and data quality standards Support the design of the future-state consolidation process, including any tooling, mapping tables, or reporting bridges required to reconcile local and consolidated views YOU BRING TO PELOTON BA/BS degree in Accounting/Finance or related field CPA preferred (or equivalent) 8+ years of relevant experience in accounting, finance transformation, or reporting at a public company and/or external audit of public companies. Public company experience is required Hands-on SAP ECC experience is required, including a working knowledge of the FI/CO module, master data structures (chart of accounts, cost centers, profit centers, internal orders), and how master data drives sub-ledger and reporting outcomes Demonstrated experience leading or contributing to a financial master data redesign, chart of accounts redesign, or ERP finance transformation program Experience or strong familiarity with AI/LLM-enabled finance tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT/Claude for data analysis, or AI-driven reconciliation modules inside major ERPs/EPMs) Experience supporting or enabling consolidations into a parent company's reporting environment, including intercompany, elimination, and mapping conventions Previous participation in existing internal control programs; strong understanding of SOX implications of master data and system changes Data analytics experience preferred; comfort working with large data sets and reporting tools to validate and communicate the impact of master data changes Project management skills — effective consultation, interpersonal, prioritization of topics/issues, and organization. Experience leading cross-functional transformation workstreams is strongly preferred Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical data model decisions into business-relevant impacts Must be a highly organized, detail-oriented self-starter with the ability to work independently and within a team environment Ability to work effectively with all levels of an organization, from analyst to executive, and across accounting, IT, FP&A, and parent-company stakeholders An objective, independent, mature, unbiased individual with the highest integrity Superior problem-solving skills and ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines #
